name: Orion
tagline: Browse with WebKit, built-in tracker blocking, and support for selected Chrome and Firefox extensions.
description:
Orion is a WebKit-based browser from Kagi that emphasizes privacy, native Apple-platform behavior, and extension compatibility. It combines built-in ad and tracker blocking with support for a curated selection of Safari, Chrome, and Firefox extensions, aiming to give Mac users flexibility without adopting a Chromium browser.

Use it as a daily browser, add only the extensions that matter, and choose Kagi integrations when they suit the workflow. Its native engine and privacy-first defaults make it interesting for users who want an alternative to Safari while avoiding the telemetry and advertising models of many mainstream browsers.

## Features

- Browse with the native WebKit engine on macOS, iPhone, and iPad.
- Use built-in ad blocking, anti-tracking, and the developer’s stated zero-telemetry browsing model.
- Install selected Safari, Chrome, and Firefox extensions, including a curated set of guaranteed-working extensions.
- Configure browser behavior and integrate available Kagi search, translation, and browsing services.
- Support the user-funded product through Orion Plus when its current subscription or lifetime-license model is appropriate.

## Where it fits

Orion fits privacy-conscious Mac users who want more extension flexibility than Safari while staying close to WebKit. It can be a strong personal browser after its extension and site compatibility are tested against your real work.

Do not assume every extension or web app will behave exactly as it does in Chrome or Firefox. Keep another browser available during a transition, particularly for critical work systems.

## Privacy and requirements

Kagi describes Orion as a zero-telemetry browser with built-in blocking. Browsing still reveals data to visited sites, search providers, extensions, and any enabled sync or Orion+ service. Chrome and Firefox extensions can request broad access and may not behave exactly as they do in their original engines, so review permissions and compatibility before trusting a critical workflow.

## Pricing

Orion includes a free tier. Plus $5/month, $50/year, or $150 lifetime.
